newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ports of Auck looks for strong 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Ports of Auck looks for strong 2nd half.

text.p: New Zealand's largest ports operator Ports of Auckland Ltd, said on Tuesday it was looking forward to a solid second half year, although trading conditions would continue to be tight.
Earlier, the company reported a fall in its half year net surplus after tax to NZ$17.4 million, from $24.5 million in the corresponding period in 1995.

The company said that adjusted for discontinued activities in property and Westhaven, the ongoing operating profit after tax was $17.0 million, compared to $16.9 million for the six months to the end of 1995.
Ports of Auckland said it continued to achieve steady growth in cargo volumes in spite of difficult trading conditions during the first half of the year.

Chief Executive Geoff Vazey said total tonnage through the port rose eight percent to 5.4 million tonnes from five million tonnes in the 1995 half year. Container volumes rose six percent during the period, to nearly 219,000 TEUs (20-foot equivalent units) and breakbulk cargo increased 11 percent to 1.9 million tonnes. Ship calls rose three percent to 1,158.
Vazey said it was pleasing to be able to report that operational performance in the port continued to improve during a difficult trading period.

"This half year was unusual in that the first quarter was very dull, while the second quarter saw an increase in activity. The first quarter was clearly affected by uncertainty as a result of the election, the high exchange rate and economic conditions," the company said.
"Importers held back on building up summer stocks until October, then there was a very strong flow of imports through to December."
